about.title: San Dimas Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: San Dimas households rely on countless products every day, from car parts driven along SR-57 and SR-210 to appliances, tools, and consumer goods bought at local shops. When one of these items is defectively designed, poorly manufactured, or missing an adequate warning, the resulting injury can be serious and sudden. California law generally allows an injured person to pursue a strict liability claim without proving the manufacturer was careless — only that the product was defective and that the defect caused harm. This matters in a community like San Dimas, where families and commuters alike depend on the reliability of everyday goods. If you were hurt by a product, keeping the item and any packaging can matter a great deal. LawProactive offers a free way to connect with an independent California attorney who can review what happened and explain your options, with no upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why San Dimas Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Path
items.desc: Because California often applies strict liability to defective products, you may not need to prove the manufacturer was negligent — just that the defect caused your injury.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which may widen the options available to pursue a claim.

items.title: Preserving Evidence Matters Early On
items.desc: Since the product itself is often central to proving a defect, connecting with an attorney early can help ensure that key evidence isn't lost or discarded.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Under California's strict liability approach, you generally only need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury. This differs from many other injury claims that require proof of negligence.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to keep the product, its packaging, and any receipts or manuals exactly as they were at the time of the injury. This evidence can be important to an attorney evaluating your case, so avoid repairing or discarding it.

items.question: Does San Dimas have specific risks tied to product injuries?
items.answer: San Dimas sees regular travel along corridors like SR-57, SR-210, and Arrow Highway, where vehicle part failures can contribute to collisions. Public crash records for the most recent year show 139 injury collisions and 204 people injured, some of which may involve defective components rather than driver error.

items.answer: LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm, and we don't charge you anything to find an independent attorney. Attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
